bug_semantics: Ech0 access tokens created with expiry=never (NEVER_EXPIRY, duration 0) are signed as JWTs with no exp claim. jwt/v5 and JWTAuthMiddleware accept that token, so a stolen bearer stays cryptographically valid until JWT_SECRET rotation. Three independent revocation paths then fail for this token class: AuthHandler.Logout dereferences claims.ExpiresAt.Time and panics on the nil field so the JTI never reaches the blacklist; AuthRepository.RevokeToken returns immediately when remainTTL <= 0; SettingService.DeleteAccessToken deletes only the metadata row and does not blacklist the JTI. Finite-expiry tokens can still age out; never-expire tokens cannot.
